newsitem.title: GERMANY: MAS ups Germany-KL capacity by 70 pct.
newsitem.headline: MAS ups Germany-KL capacity by 70 pct.

text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) said it will increase passenger seat capacity to Germany by 70 percent by the end of 1997.
The airline will introduce brand-new 278-seat Boeing 777 aircraft on its twice-weekly Munich to Kuala Lumpur flights from June 10, a statement said.
MAS will add a fourth weekly Boeing 747-400 passenger flight between Kuala Lumpur and Frankfurt from November and will operate all four flights as direct nonstop services.
The Friday flight currently stops in Vienna and the Saturday service continues on to Amsterdam.
MAS said the massive expansion came in response to growing passenger demand in Germany and daily flights from Frankfurt were planned by 2001.
The airline saw German passenger numbers rise 12 percent to 35,000 in the April 1996-March 1997 fiscal year.
Load factors were 81 percent in economy, 64 percent in business class and 45 percent in first class.
MAS Germany cargo executive, Peter Skaryd, said the fourth Frankfurt flight would provide MAS with up to 18 tonnes worth of extra cargo capacity.

But the introduction of B777 aircraft on the twice-weekly Munich flight would not be of so much benefit to cargo since the route was previously flown with a combi aircraft with a larger freight capacity, he added.
